title: AI's Accuracy Gap: Insurance Won't Cover Its Mistakes! #shorts
description: Insurers are ditching AI liability coverage as autonomous software causes major losses. Banks fear $20M blunders from agents with no audit trail. Full transparency is the only way forward for AI in regulated industries. #AIrisk #Insurtech #Regtech #AutonomousSoftware #Cybersecurity
transcript: Accuracy gap is interesting to me. But, so it says insurance carriers refuse to cover operational losses caused by unmonitored intelligent agents. State regulators granted permission for carriers to drop AI liability coverage from standard commercial policies. Policy holders across the country now include explicit exclusions for damage caused by autonomous software. Underwriters cannot assess risk when developers fail to provide detailed execution records. Banks face catastrophic financial exposure when agents make unexplained $20 million mistakes. Regulated industries will reject autonomous tools until software offers full auditability.

top_comments.author: @CircuitSage-d5e
top_comments.text: Honestly, I wouldn't call this an insurance problem. No execution logs means you shipped a prototype. Fix observability before deploying near real money.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Exactly — calling it an insurance issue misses the point. If you don’t have execution logs you’re basically running a demo in production, especially anywhere real money moves. Get observability solid first, then talk about deployment. What’s been the biggest gap you’ve seen teams struggle with there — tracing, replay, or just getting anyone to care before something breaks?
